thread:
Maya: Alert — we're seeing a cluster of 5xx + long-tail timeouts from hosted inference in eu-west-1 starting ~09:10 UTC. Multiple support tickets (8892, 8897) from customers reporting 502 then 504s after they extended client timeouts. Client-side retries are amplifying the surge.

Alex: On it. Can someone drop a repro curl and a trace id so I can trace through the edge and backend logs?

Support: From ticket 8892 (customer A):
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.inference/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"model":"rwd-3b","input":"hi"}'

Response: 502 after ~12s. Header x-rw-trace: trace=tx-7f9d2e. They later increased timeout and saw 504s.

Drew: I pulled tx-7f9d2e — edge accepted request, forwarded to worker p-3. Backend returned a 200 status but the response stream stalled during chunked transfer; proxy hit client timeout and translated to 502/504.

Jin: Observability note: that worker pool p-3 is showing increased socket churn. Kernel logs on p-3 hosts show EPIPE events and repeated TCP FIN/RST pairs. CPU and memory are normal.

Samir: Candidate cause: recent runtime change in r-20250719-18 tweaked keepalive handling and connection reuse. When combined with small-chunk streaming and KV prefix cache coldness the worker can block on socket read for ~10-15s.

deploy-bot: Canary deploy r-20250719-18 -> initiating rollback to r-20250719-17 for impacted pools :info:

Alex: I rolled back p-3 to r-20250719-17 and initiated graceful drain for remainder of canary. Early metrics: 5xx count down ~35% in eu-west within first 3 minutes.

Maya: Good mitigation. Hold rollback until we have a reproducible root cause and confirm customer impact. Support: send an interim note to affected customers: "We've rolled back a recent runtime change that reduced errors; we're investigating root cause and will share a timeline by EOD." :speech_balloon:

Support: Noted — outbound sent to tickets 8892/8897. Bulk notification list in progress. Billing holds requested; finance looped in.

Drew: Actionable repro I ran locally: spawn steady small prompts with tight client timeouts (5-10s), exercise cache misses on prefix layer — I can reproduce a blocked read on socket for ~11s that aligns with customer traces. Pushing a minimal harness to the warroom artifacts.

Jin: Short-term observability asks:
- add a metric: worker.socket_read_block_ms (histogram) per pool
- add trace tag with runtime version for all spans
- temporary log filter for tx-7f9d* to pull complete spans
Due: +3h for metric and temporary filter.

Samir: Drafting postmortem skeleton and customer FAQ. Early RCA hypotheses and mitigations will go into INC-20250719-45. Putting long-term items into backlog: revert keepalive change or add compatibility flag, synthetic streaming warmup in deploy pipeline, SDK backoff default improvements, gateway fail-fast circuit breaker for hung streams.

incident-bot: Created follow-up ticket INC-20250719-45 for postmortem, assigned to Samir (owner).

Maya: Immediate owners & SLAs:
- Alex: continue rollback for at least 2 hours, monitor 5xx p95 and tail; escalate if >10% above baseline.
- Drew: deliver minimal repro harness and trace capture (+6h).
- Jin: add socket-read metric + temp alert (p95 > 2000ms) (+3h).
- Samir: PM postmortem skeleton + customer FAQ (+8h).
- Support: notify affected customers, coordinate billing holds.

Alex: Metrics update (5m after rollback): 5xx rate in eu-west-1 down 47%, avg latency back to baseline, p99 still elevated (~+8%). Keeping rollback and watching for relapse.

Drew: Pushed log excerpt to warroom bucket: "worker p-3: chunked response stalled at read(offset=0x1b) duration=11.2s" — path: s3://warroom/INC-20250719-45/logs/8892-traces.log

Support: Customer note templates updated and saved to /docs/incidents/templates/hosted-5xx-interim.md. Finance confirmed pause on credits until postmortem clarifies impact.

Maya: Closing active war-room cadence for now. Keep this thread for status updates and paste any postmortem drafts here. If anything blocks service or customers, escalate in #oncall and ping me. Thanks. :lock:
